claims.statement: The default DeepAgentState messages channel uses DeltaChannel with the message-delta reducer; the reducer coerces raw inputs, updates or removes messages by ID, honors remove-all, and handles absent replay state as empty.

create_deep_agent resolves the model and harness profile, selects a default StateBackend, partitions inline and graph_id-based remote subagents, and delegates the final assembled graph to LangChain create_agent with execution dependencies and Deep Agents metadata.

The main middleware stack has protected filesystem and optional inline-subagent scaffolding, parent notification, summarization, patching, and optional remote-subagent support; caller middleware is merged between two profile-exclusion passes, and excluded-tool filtering is last.

A custom main state schema is forwarded to declarative inline subagents, while private schema fields are registered with installed SubAgentMiddleware instances so those keys are not returned across task delegation.

AsyncSubAgentMiddleware is independent of synchronous task delegation: it validates remote subagent names, mode, and update strategy, exposes background-task tools, and persists task identifiers in async_tasks; polling hooks run only on the asynchronous path.

A new caller ModelFallbackMiddleware is inserted before the main stack tail, allowing it to catch the final default ModelRefusalMiddleware; tests verify fallback succeeds, while default main refusal raises and profile exclusion returns the raw refusal response.

CompiledSubAgent runnables remain opaque to SDK stack construction, but SubAgentMiddleware converts ModelRefusalError or a refusal-bearing structured-output validation error from either synchronous or asynchronous child execution into a retry-warning task result; declarative child refusal behavior is covered end to end.

The task middleware validates unique child names and supported isolated or fork modes, gives isolated children only the delegated description, and builds fork history from the parent's effective summarized conversation while preventing recursive task delegation.

Task delegation excludes special and registered private state for isolated and compiled child transfer, while declarative forks retain compatible private state to rebuild the parent stack; returns contain only changed non-excluded updates plus a ToolMessage, and concurrent child writers need reducers for custom fields.

Filesystem permissions are ordered first-match rules for read and write calls; deny is enforced by FilesystemMiddleware, interrupt rules are synthesized into scoped HumanInTheLoopMiddleware predicates, and user interrupt settings override generated settings per tool.

FilesystemBackend virtual mode anchors paths under root_dir and blocks traversal or resolved escapes, while non-virtual mode allows absolute paths and relative traversal outside that root; virtual mode is not process isolation.

Focused subagent tests cover mode validation, default task-tool registration, declarative dynamic structured output, compiled-subagent schema rejection, fork prompt, state, recursion, and checkpoint-namespace behavior.
create_deep_agent binds its selected backend to caller middleware that implements BackendConsumer, and also binds declarative child middleware before child compilation.

The main prompt places caller instructions before profile base and suffix material, preserving a caller SystemMessage's content blocks by appending profile text as a separate text block; tool description overrides are applied before assembly.

A declarative subagent is assembled with its own resolved model profile and core/tail middleware, while a fork uses the parent's final system prompt and passes fork-specific instructions in the delegated task message to preserve the inherited prompt prefix.

The SDK automatically adds a general-purpose inline child unless the active profile disables it or an inline child already uses that name; without any inline child, no synchronous task middleware is installed.
create_sub_agent adds child human approval middleware when configured and ensures UnsupportedContentMiddleware before delegating child graph compilation to LangChain create_agent.

The assembled main graph passes response format, context schema, checkpointer, store, debug, name, cache, and the base state schema to LangChain create_agent, then configures recursion_limit 9999 and Deep Agents integration/version metadata.

Provider prompt-caching middleware is appended to SDK-built main and declarative-child stacks: Anthropic caching is lazily imported only for Anthropic requests, while Bedrock and Fireworks caching is optional, class-cached, and instantiated afresh for each stack.

When a task invokes a compiled LangGraph child, it streams checkpoint events and puts the actual saved checkpoint namespace in the result ToolMessage artifact; no saved checkpoint yields no artifact, while a non-graph runnable falls back to the parent task namespace.
